subject: Proposal: Renewal + Scaled Commit with Price Stability Guard
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@helixpay.com>, procurement@helixpay.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Renewal + Scaled Commit with Price Stability Guard

Hi Amit —

Great to connect last week. Per our conversation we've put together a concise renewal proposal that tries to balance HelixPay's need for predictable unit economics while keeping you cost-efficient as usage scales. Key highlights in the attached PDF:

- 12-month renewal with three-tier commit bands (Base / Growth / Surge) mapped to discounted unit rates.
- Price Stability Guard: a 6-month price hold on the Base tier for customers who commit to a minimum monthly GPU-hour baseline.
- Bridging credits: one-time $40k credit to offset churn transition costs and cover migration spike in Q3.
- Optional burst pool for seasonal spikes billed at a capped premium rate.

I attached the full proposal and a simple model (price-model-breakdown.xlsx). Please review and let me know if we should walk through the model together — happy to do a 30-min call early next week to run scenarios.

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm interest in the price-hold structure (yes/no)
2) Share any internal procurement timing/contract constraints
3) If helpful, we can add a clause for a 90-day true-up window for actual vs committed usage.

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0123 | david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2027-08-11_HelixPay_proposal_v1.pdf, price-model-breakdown.xlsx

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@helixpay.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@helixpay.com
Date: 2027-08-11T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Renewal + Scaled Commit with Price Stability Guard

David —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear model. A few items from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement: we generally can't accept a 6-month absolute price hold without a minimum annual spend guarantee. Can you convert the price-hold to a conditional hold tied to an annualized commit?
- Engineering: can you confirm the burst pool latency/throughput SLAs and whether the burst pool uses isolated GPUs? Need to know if it affects our architecture.
- Can we get a marked-up contract (redlines) to start legal review?

We'll be on a procurement review on 2027-08-18; if we have a marked-up doc by then it speeds approval.

Amit
VP, Platform Engineering
HelixPay

Subject: Re: Proposal: Renewal + Scaled Commit with Price Stability Guard

Amit —

Thanks, good questions. Quick answers below and attaching a redlined doc for legal review.

- Price-hold mechanics: we can convert the 6-month unconditional hold into a "Conditional Price Guard" that requires a 70% utilization of the committed baseline across the renewal term (annualized). If utilization drops below 70% for the term we'll revert to standard indexed pricing with a 30-day notice.
- Burst pool: shared burst pool on dedicated capacity with a guaranteed priority queue; SLA: 95th percentile token latency under typical workloads will match your current baseline. For guaranteed isolation we can provision an isolated burst pool as an add-on (higher unit rate) — details in the model.
- Attached: redlines_helixpay_v2.docx (initial legal-friendly markup).

If procurement wants the annual spend guarantee, we can model a blended minimum ARR threshold that triggers a lower Base tier. I'll loop Ben on that ask.

Would you like a short call Tues 8/17 10:00am PT to align before your procurement review?

Best,
David

Attachments: redlines_helixpay_v2.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelixPay pricing mechanics — internal approval request

David — forwarding for visibility and quick approval on the conditional guard and one-time credit.

Notes (internal):
- We can accept conditional price guard if HelixPay signs up for the blended minimum ARR of $480k/year (equates to the Base tier). That preserves unit economics and limits downside.
- One-time bridging credit of $40k is approved for onboarding; suggest tying credit to milestone (data migration complete / production cutover).
- If they request isolated burst capacity we should price at +45% over shared burst unit rate. Approve with that caveat.

Marissa / Grace, flag if you see legal/CS concerns. If all good, David should send an updated proposal and a DocuSign link with the blended ARR clause and milestone for the credit.

-Ben

Amit / HelixPay procurement —

Per our internal approvals, here's an updated and executable path:

- Conditional Price Guard: price hold tied to annualized commit utilization >= 70%. If met, Base tier rates are held for first 6 months. Clause added to section 3.2.
- Blended minimum ARR: $480,000/year as the contract minimum to enable the price guard (see contract section 2.1).
- Bridging credit: $40,000 applied as a one-time credit at cutover milestone (data migration confirmed).
- Burstable capacity: shared option included; isolated burst add-on priced at +45% unit rate.

I've uploaded the signed-ready agreement to DocuSign and included the link below. Please review the updated redlines and sign by 2027-08-20 to meet your procurement window. If you want a short alignment call tomorrow 8/14 at 10am PT I can host with Ben and Marissa.
